name: Bitcoin USD
oneLiner: BtcUSD is BTCfi's overcollateralized USD stablecoin minted from BTC variants (WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, native BTC) via Liquity-style CDP vaults.
collateral: Overcollateralized Bitcoin (WBTC, BTCB, cbBTC, native BTC) via CDP vaults

oracleRisk.summary: BTCFi documents 50% maximum LTV and liquidation risk, while Bifrost publishes native WBTC and BTCB price feeds; BTCFi's own docs do not prove which feed is wired into BtcUSD or document liquidation recovery and oracle-failure handling.

branchApplicability.rationale: BtcUSD is minted against Bitcoin collateral and therefore requires an oracle/liquidation branch review. The public BTCFi documentation describes one Bifrost-side mint workflow but does not expose separate market contracts or prove distinct collateral engines, so the documented collateral set is represented as one grouped branch and retained as opaque.

branches.label: BTCFi Bifrost Bitcoin collateral
branches.summary: BTCFi exposes a single Bifrost-side BtcUSD borrowing workflow, but its docs do not identify the price-feed contract consumed by the collateral and liquidation logic.

feeds.path: Undocumented collateral price input -> BtcUSD LTV and liquidation checks; Bifrost's published WBTC/BTCB feeds are candidates, not proven BTCFi wiring

branches.fallbackBehavior: BTCFi's public documentation does not describe staleness checks, a secondary oracle, or the behavior taken when its collateral-price source is unavailable.

collateralParameters.note: The BTCFi mint guide says users may mint up to 50% of collateral value and warns of liquidation at the liquidation threshold, but it does not publish a separate liquidation-ratio value.

branches.liquidationMechanism: The BTCFi mint and repay guides warn that positions reaching the liquidation threshold can be liquidated, but do not document who executes liquidation, the sale or offset sequence, or any execution delay.
branches.backstop: No Stability Pool, insurance reserve, debt auction, or other liquidation backstop is identified in the reviewed BTCFi documentation.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: The reviewed BTCFi documentation does not specify an oracle-failure pause, emergency shutdown, or how collateral shortfall and residual bad debt would be allocated.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Base block 48644528, the BtcUSD proxy points to verified ERC20_Bridged implementation 0x6e9070b8a8dbbc6cad6b6d029a5c6f6a653b74a9 and is unpaused. Its source gives every owner or admin authority to call set_blacklists(address[], bool), and transfer hooks reject both blacklisted senders and recipients; set_pause(bool) stops all token transfers. Current owners are 0x26FcE52a077b4f1dbD7C920b6f23a1D9d18DdDbE and 0xf98e8601A1eEF3BCE943f9B002e83Db8a0951Aa5, and current admin is 0x4F7aB59b5AC112970F5dD66D8a7ac505c8E5e08B; the latter owner successfully simulated both control calls through the proxy without broadcasting state. At Bifrost block 36763950, native BtcUSD reports paused=false, owner/defaultAdmin 0xa4247099c1462f9D9121a1809D001c1a6cC70dD5 has DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, and the runtime exposes pause/unpause; an unprivileged pause call reverts for the missing default-admin role. The Bifrost explorer did not expose verified source or ABI, so this does not assert native blacklist semantics, but both deployments have direct holder-transfer restriction surfaces.

mintAuthority.summary: BtcUSD on Base is an ERC20_Bridged (Vyper) contract whose canonical issuance lives on the Bifrost network. The Base bridge token has 2 owners: a contract (0x26fce52a..., not a Safe) and an EOA (0xf98e8601...). The native BtcUSD token on Bifrost is a non-proxy mint/burn contract owned by EOA 0xa4247099...; the CDP vault system contracts are publicly undocumented, so the owner EOA is the observable native mint authority.

sources.label: BtcUSD Bifrost token on Bifrost explorer

controls.evidence: 2026-07-20 via the Bifrost public EVM RPC (public-01.mainnet.bifrostnetwork.com/bifrost, now reachable): the native BtcUSD token 0x6906ccda405926fc3f04240187dd4fad5df6d555 is a 13.9KB non-proxy contract carrying mint()/burn() selectors whose owner() returns this EOA (no contract code). BTCfi's Liquity-v1-style CDP vault system contracts are not publicly documented and the token source is unverified, so the observable mint authority on Bifrost is this owner EOA; no separate vault contract could be identified or bounded.

controls.label: BtcUSD Base bridge owner contract
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, get_owners() on the ERC20_Bridged token returned this contract as one of two current owners. The verified bridge implementation permits token owners to mint bridged BtcUSD directly; the owner contract is not verified as a Safe or bounded multisig.

controls.label: BtcUSD Base bridge owner EOA
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, get_owners() on the ERC20_Bridged token returned this EOA as one of two current owners. The verified bridge implementation permits token owners to mint bridged BtcUSD directly.

controls.label: BtcUSD Base proxy admin (unverified contract)
controls.evidence: At Base block 48621895, the EIP-1967 admin slot of the BtcUSD bridge proxy returned this deployed contract and the implementation slot returned 0x6e9070b8. 2026-07-20 follow-up: the admin is a 10.25KB contract whose slot-0 owner reads as EOA 0xf9d5bd4013c955175185e406b407d5cee90b0001 (no contract code), so the upgrade authority chain resolves to that EOA; the admin contract itself remains source-unverified, so its delay and signer policy are unknown.

review.evidence: At Base block 48621895: BtcUSD (0xe4b20925...) is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy with EIP-1967 admin 0x55506bcc5fa9b2e702848aa110b5a6987a735060 and implementation 0x6e9070b8a8dbbc6cad6b6d029a5c6f6a653b74a9. get_owners() returned 0x26fce52a (contract) and 0xf98e8601 (EOA), both direct bridge-token mint owners. 2026-07-20 follow-up resolved both prior open questions: the Bifrost public EVM RPC (public-01.mainnet.bifrostnetwork.com/bifrost) is reachable, and the native BtcUSD token 0x6906ccda405926fc3f04240187dd4fad5df6d555 reads as a non-proxy mint/burn contract owned by EOA 0xa4247099c1462f9d9121a1809d001c1a6cc70dd5 (the CDP vault system contracts remain publicly undocumented and unverified, so the owner EOA is the observable mint authority); and the Base proxy admin's slot-0 owner reads as EOA 0xf9d5bd4013c955175185e406b407d5cee90b0001, resolving its ownership chain.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: BtcUSD/BTCFi relies on Bifrost cross-chain technology for collateral movement across networks. Bifrost bridge documentation describes a cross-chain bridge service rather than a native issuer-only route, so Pharos scores this as external validated-network exposure.
bridgeRouteRisk.reviewer: Codex bridge route review; Kimi P2 control cohort dc-5 (lead usd1-world-liberty-financial)

routes.reviewNote: On-chain 2026-07-20: this Base ERC20_Bridged proxy is the Bifrost bridge representation of native Bifrost BtcUSD; get_owners() returns bridge mint owners 0x26fce52a077b4f1dbd7c920b6f23a1d9d18dddbe (contract) and 0xf98e8601a1eef3bce943f9b002e83db8a0951aa5 (EOA). The bridge controller for the representation is the owner contract; the proxy admin 0x55506bcc5fa9b2e702848aa110b5a6987a735060 is owned by EOA 0xf9d5bd4013c955175185e406b407d5cee90b0001.

On-chain 2026-07-20 via the Bifrost public EVM RPC: this is the native BTCfi BtcUSD token (non-proxy, mint/burn selectors present, owner() = EOA 0xa4247099c1462f9d9121a1809d001c1a6cc70dd5) on the canonical CDP issuance chain; no bridge control carries the claim.
